published_prior_art.cite: OberReynolds2023: generic sharp intervals for moments of joint potential-outcome laws via optimal transport; Strassen1965: support-constrained coupling existence.
LuDingDasgupta2018: scalar support-collapse analysis; additive-cost constancy on a transportation polytope is standard transport linear algebra.
JiLeiSpector2023 gives covariate-assisted OT tightening, but no located result gives the roster-vector CRT three-contract hierarchy and common-active-cut equality characterization.
LuDingDasgupta2018, Proposition 2: sharp scalar strict-benefit bounds on a finite chain.
JiLeiSpector2023 supplies uniformly valid OT-bound inference for independent sampling; FangSantos2019 supplies the directionally differentiable resampling framework.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1 / related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: The literature omits OberReynolds2023, an accessible theorem-text preprint deriving sharp intervals for joint-potential-outcome functionals through optimal transport with root-n estimation and inference; it is materially closer than the cited generic references and must be distinguished explicitly.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 4 and honest_scope
soundness_flags.one_line: The claim that two binary coordinates scalarize through the three tiers given by the number of favorable coordinates is false: (1,0) and (0,1) occupy the same tier but are incomparable in the product order, so strict Pareto benefit cannot factor through that scalar tier.

soundness_flags.label: ass:l2-learnability / def:inference-model
soundness_flags.one_line: Membership of the law class depends on an unspecified random learner sequence \(\widetilde\mu_{a,s,G}\) and \(o_P(1)\), rather than a primitive law property; state learnability existentially as a property of \(\mu_{a,s}\) and make the selected cross-fitted learner an estimator-side input with uniform conditions.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics 43(5), 2018
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines strict benefit \(h=\Pr\{Y(1)>Y(0)\}\), gives its sharp scalar ordinal bounds, and states endpoint constructions in the supplement.
The paper gives a model-agnostic OT-duality approach for partially identified causal estimands, uniformly valid randomized-experiment inference, and multiplier-bootstrap-based model selection.
The paper defines cluster-pair and individual-pair generalized causal estimands, estimates them with weighted clustered U-statistics, and derives cross-fitted efficient inference.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 119(548), 2024
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper targets cluster-average and individual-average CRT effects with flexible covariate adjustment and cluster-size variation, proving consistency, asymptotic normality, and efficiency under nuisance consistency.

The paper shows full differentiability is necessary and sufficient for ordinary-bootstrap consistency under Gaussian limits and proposes a consistent alternative for directionally differentiable maps.

The preprint states that sharp identified sets for moments of the joint distribution of potential outcomes are intervals whose endpoints are optimal-transport values, and proposes root-n estimators and inference.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Delete the two-binary scalarization claim and replace it with an explicit \(2\times2\) diamond witness; reserve the genuinely non-chain worked example for \(2\times3\) and show its capacity cannot be reproduced by any rank-tier coarsening.

Add OberReynolds2023 to related work and state a strict delta beyond generic OT: a roster-vector CRT information-contract theorem with an explicit finite non-scalar witness and a result not implied merely by evaluating a generic transport program.

Move learner selection out of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}\), specify a cluster-fold learner and uniform approximation/variance-estimation conditions, then formulate the tied-cut coverage target over that operational estimator class.

recommended_next_step: Revise the false product-order sanity claim, repair the nonprimitive inference-model condition, and redraft novelty against OberReynolds2023 before advancing to Stage 0.
